failing_examples.q35: Article 175A was first inserted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024, section 7. The source also notes that some later text was substituted by the Constitution (Twenty-Seventh Amendment) Act, 2025, section 20, but the article itself was inserted in 2024. (Article 175A)
failing_examples.q38:
Article 25A is part of the Constitution as a fundamental right in Part II, Chapter 1, and it states that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to children aged five to sixteen years. (Article 25A)

The sources provided do not say when or by which amendment Article 25A was inserted into the Constitution. They only give the current text of Article 25A. (Article 25A)
failing_examples.q39: Article 2A became part of the Constitution because the Objectives Resolution, reproduced in the Annex, was made a substantive part of the Constitution by Article 2A itself. It says that the principles and provisions set out in the Objectives Resolution “are hereby made substantive part of the Constitution and shall have effect accordingly.” (Article 2A)
failing_examples.q41: Article 11 was added by the Constitution (Third Amendment) Act, 1975, section 2. The source does not give the exact insertion date, only the amendment act and section. (Article 11)
failing_examples.q43: The sources provided do not say when Article 140A was inserted into the Constitution. They only give the current text of Article 140A. (Article 140A)
